key_insight: An online evolutionary machine-learning framework can better account for neural activity drift and improve long-term seizure prediction from continuous intracranial EEG.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support more realistic patient-specific seizure forecasting in drug-resistant epilepsy, potentially reducing implanted channels while preserving predictive performance.
method: Analyzed a new continuous long-term stereoelectroencephalography dataset from 16 patients over 664.9 hours with 121 seizures.
Compared offline pipeline choices, then tested the best-performing setup in a pseudo-prospective online framework under realistic class imbalance.
Evolved 1,000 candidate models per patient and reduced input channels using patient-specific epileptogenic network targeting.
evidence_signal: Offline AUROC fell from 90% to 57.9% in online testing, but the evolutionary framework achieved complete event-level seizure prediction in 75% of patients and captured all but one seizure in 87.5%.
watch_item: This is a proof-of-concept framework on a specialized intracranial EEG dataset, so real-world deployment will require external validation, robust drift handling, and careful clinical integration.
paper_title: Countering Neural Activity Drift: Sustained Long-term Seizure Prediction Using an Evolutionary Machine-Learning Framework on Continuous Intracranial EEG
